name: Palopegteriparatide
route: Once-daily injection under the skin from a prefilled pen
mechanism: A slowly releasing form of PTH(1-34) that replaces the missing parathyroid hormone steadily across the day

article.summary: Palopegteriparatide (Yorvipath) is a once-daily, long-acting parathyroid hormone for adults with hypoparathyroidism. In a phase 3 trial most people no longer needed standard calcium and active vitamin D therapy.
article.takeaway: Palopegteriparatide is a long-acting form of parathyroid hormone (PTH) for adults whose parathyroid glands do not make enough of it. It is injected once a day and releases active PTH slowly from an inert carrier, which helps keep calcium steady. In the PaTHway trial, 79% of people on it met a combined goal of normal calcium and independence from active vitamin D and high-dose calcium, versus 5% on placebo.[^1] Its main risks are swings in blood calcium and a theoretical risk of bone tumors.[^2]
glance: Replacing missing PTH so calcium stays in range
One injection a day under the skin from a prefilled pen
PaTHway phase 3 trial: 26 weeks versus placebo, then 52 weeks

blocks.text: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) keeps blood calcium in a narrow range by acting on bone and kidneys. In hypoparathyroidism the glands make too little PTH, so calcium falls. The usual treatment, calcium plus active vitamin D, treats the numbers but does not restore normal PTH action.[^1]

Palopegteriparatide is a prodrug: PTH(1-34), the active fragment, is temporarily attached to an inert carrier through a linker. In the body the linker breaks down slowly, releasing active PTH over the day.[^2]

Yorvipath is approved for hypoparathyroidism in adults. It was not studied for acute post-surgical hypoparathyroidism, and its dosing scheme was tested only in adults whose calcium was first stabilized with calcium and active vitamin D.[^2]

rows: Combined goal met by 79% (48 of 61) vs 5% (1 of 21) on placebo[^1]
81% met the goal; 95% no longer needed conventional therapy; none needed active vitamin D[^3]

blocks.text: Participants also reported better symptoms and well-being, and 24-hour urine calcium, a kidney-stone risk marker, came down.[^1][^3]

Yorvipath is a once-daily injection under the skin from a pen. The label caps the daily dose at 30 micrograms and stresses using only one injection per day, because combining two makes the delivered dose less predictable and can swing calcium. Calcium and vitamin D doses are adjusted around it using blood tests.[^2]

items: **Calcium swings:** serious high or low blood calcium can occur, so calcium is checked periodically[^2]
**Allergic reactions,** including anaphylaxis, have been reported with PTH analogs[^2]
**Bone tumor risk:** a potential risk of osteosarcoma, so it is not recommended for people at increased risk[^2]
**Digoxin:** high calcium can raise the risk of digoxin toxicity[^2]

blocks.text: In PaTHway most adverse events were mild or moderate.[^1]

evidence.label: Strong: randomized phase 3 with 52-week follow-up
evidence.text: PaTHway was randomized and placebo-controlled for 26 weeks, then followed participants to 52 weeks.[^1][^3] It measured calcium and quality of life; fractures and very long-term outcomes were not its focus.

faq.q: How is it different from Natpara?
faq.a: [Natpara](/peptides/parathyroid-hormone) was full-length PTH(1-84). Yorvipath is a long-acting prodrug of PTH(1-34). Takeda's final notice said Natpara shipments ended after December 31, 2025 and pointed prescribers to Yorvipath's prescribing information.[^4]
The current label covers adults only.[^2]

faq.q: Does it replace calcium and vitamin D?
faq.a: Many people in PaTHway no longer needed standard therapy (93% at 26 weeks and 95% at 52 weeks), but doses are adjusted individually.[^1][^3]
